transit.label: Existing network
transit.body: The existing métro stops and bus lanes establish where service is concentrated. The team used this network as the starting point for comparing tram routes.

transit.label: Earlier alignment
transit.body: The capstone describes an earlier alignment on Honoré-Beaugrand, L’Assomption and Hochelaga that the 2024 PSE study rejected. Frequent driveways and a narrow right-of-way constrained Honoré-Beaugrand. Steep grades on L’Assomption added an engineering challenge.

transit.label: Proposed Viau alignment
transit.body: The team proposed a route along Hochelaga and Viau, with a tunnel through the steeper section. The aim was to improve east–west access and connect redevelopment areas to transit more equitably.

slopes.label: Viau Street
slopes.body: The team used the Viau Street profile to identify where a tunnel could help the tram manage the terrain. The 6% reference line gives both profiles a common point of comparison.

slopes.label: Assomption Boulevard
slopes.body: Parts of the boulevard approach a 14% grade. Read against the same 6% reference line, the profile shows why a surface alignment here would need further engineering analysis.

development.label: 3D development
development.heading: Reconnect the district
development.body: The 3D model shows how the proposed blocks fit into the surrounding city. It establishes the overall street pattern before the plan turns to individual plots.

development.label: Blocks & green space
development.alt: Proposed plots, green spaces, and built form
development.heading: Make room within the blocks
development.body: The proposal divides large industrial parcels into smaller blocks. Green spaces within them would support green infrastructure and provide shared outdoor space for a denser mix of uses.

development.label: Street hierarchy
development.heading: Give the blocks a street network
development.body: The team retained key streets and introduced a hierarchy of new connections for walking and other modes. A shared street intersects Pierre de Coubertin and Hochelaga. The proposed streets target a typical width of 28.4 metres.

statistics.title: Proposed development scenario
statistics.note: Proposed scenario, not completed development. The report separately lists 13,574 total dwellings in its table; it does not reconcile this with the 12,574 new dwellings in its narrative.
